title: How Personality Traits Shape LLM Risk-Taking Behaviour

live_model.evidence: Model-version table: "GPT-4o gpt-4o (2024-08-06)...GPT-4 Turbo gpt-4 (turbo-2024-04-09)"; Fig. 3: "(a) Claude 3 Sonnet, (b) GPT-4o, (c) GPT-4 Turbo" CPT estimates

prompt.location: Sec. 3-4 (personality-prompting and CPT gamble-choice methodology described); exact system-prompt templates not confirmed verbatim in the excerpts read
prompt.note: LLMs are prompted to adopt Big Five personality trait levels, then presented with monetary gambles; Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT) parameters (alpha, beta, lambda) are fit to their choices.

claim.metric: CPT risk-aversion parameter (alpha) under Openness-trait intervention, GPT-4-Turbo
claim.location: Figure 3(c) ("GPT-4 Turbo", 15 runs per intervention level); a nearby table gives alpha=0.52, beta=0.44, lambda=-0.30 for an Openness intervention, but the excerpt read does not unambiguously confirm this specific table belongs to GPT-4-Turbo rather than GPT-4o

data.source: Standard CPT gamble-choice paradigm (Tversky & Kahneman) and Big Five/BFI personality framework, both established public instruments

notes: GPT-4-Turbo is one of several models (with Claude 3 Sonnet, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, and others) directly tested across personality-intervention levels (15 runs per level per Fig. 3). Marked 'maybe': the precise numeric CPT parameters attributable specifically to GPT-4-Turbo (as opposed to GPT-4o) were not confidently isolated in the excerpts read, and the exact prompt wording was not located verbatim.
